number.why: The served arm means, SDs and sample sizes match the source for diary-recorded sleep latency at 3 weeks in the age 65-80 subgroup. Their reconstructed unadjusted difference is -17.4 minutes. The reported adjusted difference is separately -15.6 minutes (95% CI -25.3 to -6); that confidence interval must not be attached to -17.4.

entry.why: The packet asks about adults with primary insomnia. The entry criteria explicitly establish that population. The served older subgroup also satisfies those criteria; its narrower age coverage does not make entry eligibility only partly established. The ruling conflates subgroup coverage with entry-population eligibility.

quotes.span: Men and women aged between 18 and 80 years suffering from primary insomnia according to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual for Mental Disorders (DSM-IV) criteria with sleep latency longer than 20 min were included in the study.
POPULATION: Pre-planned analysis on ITT population age 65-80

Patients still eligible after the 2-week placebo run-in and who were compliant with respect to treatment, had a negative drug screen and correctly completed study assessment forms were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either PRM 2 mg or placebo for 3 weeks in a double-blind manner.

missed: The material missed distinction is entry eligibility versus age-subgroup coverage, which changes ENTRY to ESTABLISHED. No additional finding changes NUMBER; agreement applies to the reconstructed 3-week effect.
